class: A field found by its HTML attributes instead of by what it is labelled, and a form submitted without checking each thing it needs was really in it
symptom: KBI Biopharma on Workday (jsrglobal.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com), 28 September: Create Account was pressed with both passwords filled and the Email Address box empty, and Workday showed an error at the top of the form. The log said 'Detected 1 fillable fields, matched 1' and then listed 'Email Address*' among the empty boxes.
site: Workday Create Account; any form whose email box is type=text and known only by its label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, placeholder or data-automation-id
root_cause: fill_create_account_form looked for the email box with its own CSS list (type=email, name/id containing email or username). Workday's box is type=text with a generated id and data-automation-id='email', so the list matched nothing, the email loop ran zero times, and nothing checked that an email had been typed before the passwords were entered and Create Account pressed. The sign-in form had a longer list of its own (_find_login_email_input): one decision written twice, and the copies had drifted apart.
why_tests_missed: Every account-form fixture used <input type='email'> or id='email', the one shape both lists already knew. No test put a label-only email box on the form, and none asserted what the form held at the moment Create Account was pressed.
fix: One finder, _email_boxes, reads what a person or a screen reader would -- label (for= or wrapping), aria-label, aria-labelledby, placeholder, name/id/autocomplete/data-automation-id -- and both the account form and the sign-in use it. The email goes in first and is checked (_email_kept); with no email box, or one that will not keep the address, neither Create Account nor Sign In is pressed. Right before Create Account the email is re-checked and re-typed if a redraw cleared it, as the passwords already were. After creating the account the agent now signs in once with the email and password instead of stopping (the owner's decision of 28 September); an emailed code is read by the existing code step, and a rejection is counted and held by login_guard.
prevention: Find every form field by its accessible name, through one shared finder per kind of field, and test it against each way a page can label a box. Before pressing a form's submit, assert that every value the form needs is in its box right now -- not that it was typed once.
